findings.statement: CXCR2 transcripts in inflamed UC come almost entirely from neutrophils in Gubatan 2026, so the Smillie 2019 attribution to T/NK clusters (where neutrophils were not captured) does not replicate (only GSE282122 agrees; Garrido-Trigo 2023 and Gubatan 2026 give myeloid). Neutrophil share of transcripts [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]. The bulk rise is mostly neutrophil influx: the fraction retained after composition adjustment is [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17], although the adjusted change stays significant (verdict partly_composition), so CXCR2 is mainly a marker of neutrophil arrival and a target only in the sense of blocking neutrophil recruitment.

CXCL8 is made by myeloid cells (macrophages in Smillie; replicated in Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122, all three agree), with neutrophils contributing most transcripts in Gubatan. The bulk increase loses significance after cell-composition adjustment: adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0525], verdict composition. This marks myeloid/neutrophil influx rather than a tissue-intrinsic change, with the caveat that adjustment can over-correct when resident cells activate.

DUOX2 is an epithelial gene (enterocytes), dominant lineage epithelial in Smillie and in all three other atlases (Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026, GSE282122; replicated), with few neutrophil transcripts. Spots deconvolved in Visium attribute it to epithelium: [gene=DUOX2; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.818], and Xenium shows epithelial neighbours enriched. The bulk change keeps a significant adjusted change (partly_composition), retained fraction [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.397], so it is a genuine epithelial tissue change.

MMP1 comes from stromal cells, mainly inflammatory fibroblasts (Smillie and Gubatan), and the stromal attribution replicates in Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122 (all three agree); neutrophils contribute little. The adjusted bulk change remains significant, retained fraction [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.438] (partly_composition), supporting a fibroblast-intrinsic change.

CHI3L1 is produced mainly by inflammatory fibroblasts in Smillie, with stromal lineage replicated in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122 but myeloid dominant in Gubatan 2026, where neutrophils carry a sizeable share of transcripts, so attribution is stromal with some myeloid/neutrophil contribution. Adjusted change stays significant (partly_composition), retained fraction [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.366].

IDO1 is made by myeloid cells (macrophages and DC1) in Smillie, replicated in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122, but Gubatan 2026 assigns it to epithelium (enterocytes), so the cell of origin is partly context dependent; neutrophils contribute little. The adjusted change stays significant (partly_composition), indicating an inducible tissue change.

CD274 (PD-L1) has diffuse expression across plasma cells, macrophages and enterocytes in Smillie (dominant myeloid lineage share only moderate), replicated in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and Gubatan 2026 but T/NK in GSE282122; neutrophils carry a large share in Gubatan. The adjusted change stays significant (partly_composition), so it reflects both influx and an in-tissue induction; attribution to a single cell type is weak.

AQP9 is neutrophil-dominated in inflamed mucosa: [gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92]. Most of its bulk rise reflects neutrophil influx (partly_composition, retained fraction [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.261], adjusted change still significant), so it is a marker of influx rather than a tissue-intrinsic target.

S100A8 is a neutrophil-derived marker: [gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]. After adjustment the change is reduced to a retained fraction of [gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.288] but remains significant (partly_composition), consistent with a neutrophil-influx marker with some tissue component.

TREM1 transcripts are largely neutrophil: [gene=TREM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.894]. The adjusted change stays significant but small (partly_composition, retained fraction [gene=TREM1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.24]), so TREM1 is chiefly an influx marker; a target role would be in infiltrating myeloid cells.

JAK2 is the only candidate examined with an intrinsic verdict: the change survives adjustment, retained fraction [gene=JAK2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.646]. Expression is diffuse (macrophages, plasma cells, B cells, enterocytes, neutrophils), without a single dominant cell type, and the Smillie lineage attribution is not given as replicated, so it supports a broad tissue-level signalling target (cytokine-JAK pathway) rather than a cell-specific one.

caveats: Smillie 2019 lacks neutrophils, so its attribution of neutrophil genes (CXCR2, CXCR1) to T/NK or macrophages is an artefact; use the Gubatan 2026 neutrophil share.
Composition adjustment uses proportions estimated from bulk biopsies and may over-correct when resident cells become activated; partly_composition genes still retain a significant adjusted change.
Shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance.
CXCR1, IL1B, IL6, CCL2, LCN2 were screened only for neutrophil share, not composition; spatial context was run only for DUOX2.
